title: Molecular foundations
description: A short retrieval session across structure, bonding, and biochemical building blocks.
subject: General chemistry

questions.question: Which subatomic particle primarily determines an element's chemical identity?
questions.explanation: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus, and it defines which element an atom is.

questions.question: In a water molecule, the bond between oxygen and hydrogen is best described as…
questions.explanation: Oxygen attracts the shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen, creating a polar covalent bond.

questions.question: Which observations are consistent with a polar molecule? Select all that apply.

options.text: It has an uneven distribution of charge.
It can interact with other dipoles.
Its bond electrons are always shared equally.
Its geometry can prevent bond dipoles from cancelling.

questions.explanation: A polar molecule has a net dipole. Uneven charge distribution, dipole interactions, and non-cancelling bond dipoles are all clues.

questions.question: A catalyst changes the equilibrium constant of the reaction it catalyses.
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions. It changes the rate, not the equilibrium constant.

questions.question: The pH of a neutral solution at 25 °C is 7.
questions.explanation: At 25 °C, neutral water has equal concentrations of H₃O⁺ and OH⁻, giving pH 7.

questions.question: What is the name of the functional group written as –OH?
questions.explanation: The –OH group is called a hydroxyl group. It is characteristic of alcohols and appears in many biomolecules.

questions.question: Complete the notation for the common phosphate ion: PO₄____⁻.
questions.explanation: The phosphate ion is PO₄³⁻, carrying an overall charge of −3.
